title: Smart Rings Explained: Oura, Galaxy Ring and More
description: Smart rings compared in plain English: Oura vs Galaxy Ring vs RingConn and Ultrahuman, subscriptions, sizing, and why some are hard to buy in the US.
h1: Smart rings explained: Oura, Galaxy Ring and the rest
intro: Smart rings track sleep and recovery without a screen on your wrist. The big differences are subscriptions, phone compatibility and, lately, patent battles.

image.alt: A rumpled bed with striped bedding in soft morning light

cardText: Oura vs Galaxy Ring vs the rest: subscriptions, sizing and US availability.

sections.html: A sensor-packed ring measures heart rate, heart-rate variability, skin temperature and movement, mostly to score your sleep and recovery. With no screen, everything happens in the phone app, and battery life is usually measured in days.

• Oura Ring 4: the category leader with the most polished app, but most insights need a paid monthly membership.
  • Samsung Galaxy Ring: no subscription, works best with Samsung Galaxy phones.
  • RingConn: a lower-priced, subscription-free option, now sold in the US under a patent licence according to reports.
  • Ultrahuman: subscription-free, but its Ring Air was hit by a US import ban after an October 2025 patent ruling in Oura’s favour. Check current availability where you live.

Always use the free sizing kit: ring sizes vary between brands and fingers swell during the day. And add up the yearly membership cost before comparing prices. A cheaper ring with a subscription can cost more over two years.

faqs.q: Do smart rings work with iPhone?
faqs.a: Oura, RingConn and Ultrahuman work with iPhone and Android. Samsung’s Galaxy Ring is designed for Android, and some features need a Samsung phone.
